title: Elmwood Insurance SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
summary: Redwood walked Elmwood through SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture, trust center access, controls mapping, SSO/RBAC, audit logs, and KMS/encryption questions. Customer requested SOC 2 report, control matrix mapping to Elmwood's checklist, and follow-up pilot for log forwarding and SSO testing.
topics: Trust Center access and evidence requests
Controls mapping spreadsheet (customer control IDs -> Redwood controls)
Encryption at rest and KMS/HSM options
Data residency and VPC/private deployment options
Next steps: share reports, schedule pilot, technical deep-dive
transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Laura from Redwood, AE on this account. Marcus, our solutions engineer, is on as well. Can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Sarah Morales: Hi, Sarah Morales, I'm CISO at Elmwood. We also have James, head of compliance, and Priya our security engineer.
[00:20] Marcus Patel: Hey team, Marcus here, SE. I'll cover the technical posture details and controls mapping.
[00:28] Laura Chen: Goal today is to run through our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 posture, show what we can share in the trust center, and map to Elmwood's requirements. Also hear what evidence you need.
[00:40] James O'Neill: Great. Our timeline is Q1 procurement; we need SOC 2 report and control mapping to support our vendor risk. Also need to validate SSO and audit log forwarding.
[00:52] Laura Chen: Understood. We'll cover what we can share immediately and what requires an NDA or attestation. To start high level: Redwood has an annual SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certificate; latest SOC 2 period ended October 2026. We host reports in the Trust Center and can provide either a read-only link or a PDF under an NDA.
[01:12] Sarah Morales: Are those reports current? And do you provide cover letters for subservice org mapping?
[01:18] Marcus Patel: Reports are current. For subservicer mapping — you mean our cloud infra? We provide an SSAE mapping section in the report and we also have a controls mapping workbook that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks, including SOC 2 criteria and ISO 27001 controls.
[01:32] Priya Reddy: Would you be able to map specific Elmwood control IDs? Our GRC wants direct mappings.
[01:38] Marcus Patel: Yes, we can produce a controls mapping spreadsheet tailored to Elmwood. Usually we provide a generic mapping first, then post-demo we can do a customer-specific mapping showing where evidence lives. That will list control owner, evidence location (trust center doc IDs), and any compensating controls.
[01:55] James O'Neill: How fast can we get that? Within two weeks?
[02:00] Laura Chen: Two weeks is reasonable. We'll include the SOC 2 report PDF (under NDA) and the mapping workbook.
[02:07] Sarah Morales: Ok. On SSO — can you confirm SAML 2.0 support and SCIM for provisioning? Also RBAC for role separation?
[02:15] Marcus Patel: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 for IdP SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Our product has an RBAC model with roles: admin, developer, auditor, and read-only. You can create org-level roles and route-specific roles. We enforce least privilege; it's configurable via the console or via API.
[02:36] Priya Reddy: Does RBAC integrate with groups from Okta? We want group-sync so we can manage access in Okta.
[02:42] Marcus Patel: Group-sync via SCIM is supported. There are a few gotchas we've seen: group name length and nested groups. We'll document the exact SCIM attributes Elmwood should expect.
[02:54] Sarah Morales: Audit logs: retention, fields included, and ability to forward to our SIEM?
[03:00] Marcus Patel: Audit logs capture token-level operations, auth events, admin actions, model deployments, and API requests metadata (timestamp, user, request_id, model, route). Default retention for hosted customers is 90 days. For enterprise we can configure extended retention or forwarding. We can forward to S3, Splunk, or an HTTP endpoint, and we support syslog/SIEM connectors via our audit-forwarder.
[03:26] James O'Neill: Is the log export encrypted in transit? What about key management?
[03:30] Marcus Patel: Exports are TLS 1.2+; we recommend mutual TLS for SIEM endpoints if you need stronger auth. For encryption at rest we use AES-256 and for customer-managed keys we support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Private deployments.
[03:52] Sarah Morales: On encryption: do you encrypt per-tenant keys or is there a shared key?
[03:57] Marcus Patel: For hosted default we manage keys per region; we also offer customer-managed keys (CMK) where Elmwood owns the KMS keys. For Dedicated/Private we can support HSM and bring-your-own-key models so keys never leave your control.
[04:10] Priya Reddy: Data residency — our policy requires PII and PHI to remain in US regions only. Can you commit to region restrictions?
[04:18] Laura Chen: Yes, we have region tagging and can pin accounts to specific regions. For Elmwood we'd set the tenancy to a US region, and with Dedicated or Private deployments we can guarantee residency.
[04:30] Sarah Morales: Any SOC 2 exceptions or open findings in last audit?
[04:34] Marcus Patel: No significant exceptions. A minor remediation item around age of some internal docs has been closed. We can surface the remediation summary in the trust center.
[04:45] James O'Neill: About trust center access — is that self-serve or do we need to request?
[04:50] Marcus Patel: We can grant read-only access to customers once the NDA is executed. There are also downloadable artifacts, and we track access logs for each trust center share.
[05:02] Sarah Morales: We will need access for our third-party risk team and our auditor.
[05:06] Laura Chen: Noted. We'll prepare a trust center guest link for Elmwood and outline what needs NDA.
[05:12] Priya Reddy: For control evidence, what's typically included? Config screenshots? GRC IDs?
[05:18] Marcus Patel: Evidence includes policy docs, configuration screenshots, architecture diagrams, penetration test summaries, and service configuration manifests. Each evidence item is tagged to a control in the mapping workbook.
[05:30] Sarah Morales: On network/security architecture, we need to know your VPC/network segmentation for private deployments.
[05:36] Marcus Patel: For Private deployments we provide a VPC design that customers manage; we produce a runbook for peering, NAT, and security groups. For Dedicated we offer private subnets and restricted egress. We'll share the network architecture diagram.
[05:52] James O'Neill: Any multi-tenant concerns? We prefer logical separation and assurance that no cross-tenant leakage can occur.
[05:58] Marcus Patel: Hosted is logically multi-tenant with strong tenancy isolation via Kubernetes namespaces, network policies, and application-level tenant checks. For the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated where you get isolated GPU pools and tenant-dedicated nodes.
[06:14] Sarah Morales: We may start with hosted for evaluation but plan Dedicated for production.
[06:18] Laura Chen: That's a common path. We'll note that in next steps.
[06:22] Priya Reddy: Can we get details on key rotation and KMS key lifecycle?
[06:28] Marcus Patel: Key rotation is supported; for Redwood-managed keys we rotate keys annually and maintain rotation history. For CMKs we rely on the customer's KMS policies and can trigger re-encryption workflows if needed.
[06:40] Sarah Morales: Pen testing: do you allow customer-led tests or is there a scope?
[06:44] Marcus Patel: We allow customer testing with a completed penetration testing request. For hosted customers we require coordination windows; for Private deployments customers can run tests on their private infra. We also publish the standard scope in the trust center.
[06:58] James O'Neill: About identity proofing: do you do SCIM provisioning logs so we can see who provisioned which users?
[07:04] Marcus Patel: Yes, provisioning events are in the audit logs. They include actor, timestamp, target attributes.
[07:10] Sarah Morales: We also need to validate administrative separation — can you show who has access to production keys?
[07:16] Marcus Patel: That's part of the evidence package; we can show KMS IAM policies (sanitized) and admin access controls. For CMK we recommend Elmwood control of customer keys.
[07:28] Priya Reddy: Is there a SOC 2 bridge letter if the report is slightly older?
[07:32] Marcus Patel: We can provide a bridge letter if necessary; however our SOC 2 ended Oct 2026 which is recent.
[07:40] Laura Chen: Let's talk about the control mapping deliverable. We'll send a CSV mapping these columns: Elmwood control ID, Elmwood control description, Redwood control ID, Redwood evidence link, status (compliant/partial), notes.
[07:56] James O'Neill: Good. Also, our procurement wants pricing impact of Dedicated and extended log retention separately.
[08:03] Laura Chen: We'll provide pricing for Dedicated and an add-on for log retention. I'll coordinate with sales ops to put that in the quote.
[08:12] Sarah Morales: For log forwarding, do you support purge requests and deletion for data subjects?
[08:18] Marcus Patel: For requests around deletion, we support data deletion APIs and can provide scripts. For logs, depending on retention, we can redact or delete records; documented in the privacy section.
[08:30] Priya Reddy: Any automated tooling for monitoring model regressions or drift for PII leakage?
[08:36] Marcus Patel: We have Redwood Optimize tooling that can surface quality regressions; for PII specifically we recommend prompt filters and tokenization at the client side. We also support prefix/KV caching controls to limit long-term storage of sensitive prompts.
[08:52] Sarah Morales: I'd like to see a technical deep-dive on the KMS and audit pipeline next week with Priya and your SE.
[08:59] Laura Chen: We can schedule a technical deep-dive. Marcus, availability?
[09:02] Marcus Patel: I'm available Monday or Tuesday next week.
[09:06] James O'Neill: Tuesday works for us.
[09:08] Laura Chen: Great. We'll do deep-dive Tuesday.
[09:12] Sarah Morales: A couple of minor clarifications — do you maintain immutable logs for audit purposes? We need tamper evidence.
[09:18] Marcus Patel: We write audit logs to append-only S3 with object versioning and optional write-once configurations for Dedicated. We can provide tamper-evidence via checksums and signed manifests.
[09:30] Priya Reddy: How do you handle encryption keys for backups?
[09:34] Marcus Patel: Backups are encrypted with the same CMK or Redwood-managed keys depending on deployment. Backup access is limited to a small set of ops roles and audited.
[09:44] Laura Chen: We're approaching time. Quick recap: Redwood will — one, share SOC 2 Type II PDF (NDA); two, provide ISO 27001 certificate and summary; three, send controls mapping workbook and customer-specific mapping within two weeks; four, grant trust center read access for Elmwood's risk and auditor; five, schedule KMS/audit-log technical deep-dive next Tuesday; six, include pricing for Dedicated and log retention in the quote.
[10:12] Sarah Morales: That aligns. One ask: can you include a short architecture doc showing tenant isolation for hosted? Our risk team needs that.
[10:20] Marcus Patel: Yes we'll include a tenant isolation diagram and manifest of isolation controls.
[10:26] James O'Neill: And evidence of annual pen test and remediation closure notes.
[10:30] Marcus Patel: We'll include the pentest summary and the remediation tracker.
[10:34] Laura Chen: Next steps we'll put in the calendar invite. Any final Qs?
[10:38] Priya Reddy: None from me.
[10:40] Sarah Morales: No, thanks.
[10:42] Laura Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet by EOD tomorrow for trust center access and get the control mapping in two weeks.
[10:50] James O'Neill: Thanks all.
[10:54] [call ends — 58:04]
next_steps: Execute NDA to receive SOC 2 PDF and trust center access
Redwood to send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate (EOD tomorrow once NDA in place)
Provide controls mapping workbook tailored to Elmwood (within 2 weeks)
Schedule technical deep-dive on KMS/audit-log pipeline (Tuesday next week)
Include Dedicated and extended log retention pricing in formal quote
action_items: Laura Chen: Send NDA template and initiate trust center guest link (due: 2026-12-30)
Marcus Patel: Produce controls mapping workbook and tenant isolation diagram (due: 2027-01-12)
Marcus Patel: Prepare pentest summary and remediation tracker for evidence (due: 2026-12-31)
Laura Chen: Coordinate Dedicated pricing and log retention add-on with sales ops (due: 2027-01-05)
